hlaunit.ieee1516e.common

Class TestFederateAmbassador

  • java.lang.Object
    • hla.rti1516e.NullFederateAmbassador
      • hlaunit.ieee1516e.common.TestFederateAmbassador
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    hla.rti1516e.FederateAmbassador

    public class TestFederateAmbassador
extends hla.rti1516e.NullFederateAmbassador
    NOTE: I have replaced all the timeout settings with a single, TestFederateAmbassador specific value (set via the get/set defaultTimeout methods). So if you see a mention of a timeout the doco for any methods, you'll know I now mean that default value.

      • waitForSyncAnnounce

        public byte[] waitForSyncAnnounce(String label)
        Waits timeout seconds for the sync point label to be announced. It it is already announced or is announced before the time out, the tag is returned. If it is not announced before the timeout, Assert.fail() will be used.

      • waitForSyncAnnounceTimeout

        public void waitForSyncAnnounceTimeout(String label)
        This method is the inverse of waitForSyncAnnounce(String) except that it is to be used when you are *NOT* expecting an announcement to be received. It will wait for a timeout to occur, and if the label is not announced before that point, the method will return happily. If the point IS announced (or has been previously announced), Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test.

      • isAnnounced

        public boolean isAnnounced(String label)
        Returns true if the given sync point has been announced, false otherwise

      • waitForSyncResult

        public boolean waitForSyncResult(String label)
        This method will wait for the given time (in seconds) until a registration result for the given sync point is received. If the timeout occurs or there is a problem ticking, a TimeoutException will be thrown. If a success message is received, true is returned, if a failure message is received, false is returned.

      • waitForSyncResult

        public void waitForSyncResult(String label,
                              boolean expectedResult)
        This method is much like waitForSyncResult(String), except that you can specify what you are expecting the result to be. If the actual result differs from that, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test.

      • waitForSynchronized

        public void waitForSynchronized(String label)
        Wait the given number of seconds for the federation to synchronize on the syncpoint with the given label.

      • waitForSynchronizedTimeout

        public void waitForSynchronizedTimeout(String label)
        The same as waitForSynchronized(String) except that it expects to fail. It will wait for a timeout period, and if that timeout is reached, the method will return happily. If the synchronized notification is reached before the timeout, Assert.fail() is used to kill the test.

      • isSynchronized

        public boolean isSynchronized(String label)
        Has the federation synchronized on the given label?

      • waitForObjectNameReservationSuccess

        public void waitForObjectNameReservationSuccess(String name)
        Block until we get a notification that the name reservation succeeded. If we told that the reservation failed, or we get no notification in time, fail the test.

      • waitForObjectNameReservationFailure

        public void waitForObjectNameReservationFailure(String name)
        Block until we get a notification that the name reservation failed. If we told that the reservation was a success, or we get no notification in time, fail the test.

      • waitForDiscovery

        public void waitForDiscovery(int instanceHandle)
        Block execution until we get a discovery of an instance with the given handle. Only wait for the given number of seconds (in timeout). If we don't discover the instance by then, throw a TimeoutException. If the instance has already been discovered, this method will return right away.

      • waitForDiscoveryTimeout

        public void waitForDiscoveryTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This method is the opposite of waitForDiscovery(int). It will wait to be notified of the creation of an instance by the given handle, but if it gets one (or the instance already exists) before the timeout, it will assert an error. If the timeout occurs, it will return happily.

      • waitForDiscoveryAs

        public void waitForDiscoveryAs(int instanceHandle,
                               int expectedClass)
        This method will block until we get a discovery callback for an object instance that has the given instanceHandle. If the discovery isn't received before a timeout, an exception will be thrown. Once we have discovered the instance, this method will validate that the object class the instance was discovered as is equal to the expectedClass. If it isn't, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test.
        Parameters:
        instanceHandle - The handle of the object instance to wait for discovery of
        expectedClass - The object class we expect to be associated with the instance when we get the discovery callback for it
        Throws:
        TimeoutException - If the discovery takes too long to turn up

      • waitForLatestDiscovery

        public TestObject waitForLatestDiscovery(int classHandle)
        THis method will block execution until either an instance of the given class handle is discovered, or the given timeout (in seconds) has elapsed. If an instance of the given class was previously discovered, it will be returned right away. As instances are discovered, they are stored in order. Thus, this method will return the oldest discovered instance of the given class first. If the timeout occurs, an exception will be thrown.
        Parameters:
        classHandle - The handle of the class to find the latest discovered instance of
        Returns:
        The latest discovered instance of the given class
        Throws:
        TimeoutException - If the timeout is up before the a suitable instance is discovered

      • waitForUpdate

        public void waitForUpdate(int instanceHandle)
        This method will block until the federate ambassador receives a callback informing it that the specified instance has been updated. If there is no update before the given timeout (in seconds), a TimeoutException will be thrown. It will always check for RO updates before it checks for TSO ones. Also, if both an RO and TSO update exists, only the first one found will be removed.

      • waitForROUpdate

        public void waitForROUpdate(int handle)
        This method will block until the federate ambassador receives a RO callback informing it that the specified instance has been updated. If there is no update before the given timeout (in seconds), a TimeoutException will be thrown. Any TSO updates received will not be considered here.

      • waitForTSOUpdate

        public void waitForTSOUpdate(int handle)
        This method will block until the federate ambassador receives a TSO callback informing it that the specified instance has been updated. If there is no update before the given timeout (in seconds), a TimeoutException will be thrown. Any RO updates received will not be considered here.

      • waitForUpdateTimeout

        public void waitForUpdateTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This is the inverse of the waitForUpdate(int) method (sort of). It will wait for an update to come through for the given instance, but it IS EXPECTING A TIMEOUT. If the timeout does occur, this method will happily return. If not, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test. It will tick() away happily while it waits.
        Parameters:
        instanceHandle - The handle of the instance to wait for an update of

      • waitForROUpdateTimeout

        public void waitForROUpdateTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This is the same as waitForUpdateTimeout(int), except that it will only check for RO updates, rather than all updates.

      • waitForTSOUpdateTimeout

        public void waitForTSOUpdateTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This is the same as waitForUpdateTimeout(int), except that it will only check for TSO updates, rather than all updates.

      • waitForProvideRequest

        public Set<Integer> waitForProvideRequest(int instanceHandle)
        This method will block until a request to update the attributes of the given object instance has been received. It will only block for the given timeout (in seconds), after which it will throw a TimeoutException if the update request has not been received. If the request is received in time, the handles requested for update will be returned.

      • waitForProvideRequestTimeout

        public void waitForProvideRequestTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This is the inverse of waitForProvideRequest(int). It expects a timeout. If a "provide update" notification is delivered before that timeout can occur, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test. If the timeout does occur, this method will return happily.

      • waitForRORemoval

        public void waitForRORemoval(int instanceHandle)
        This method will block until either the timeout it up, or we have received an RO remove callback for the given instance handle (it will tick while blocking). If the timeout runs up before we get a remove, a TimeoutException will be thrown.

      • waitForRORemovalTimeout

        public void waitForRORemovalTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This method is the inverse of waitForRORemoval(int). Rather than waiting for the removal, and then failing the test if it does not occur, it waits for the timeout to occur, erroring if a RO removal of the given instance occurs in that time.

      • waitForTSORemoval

        public void waitForTSORemoval(int instanceHandle)
        This method will block until either the timeout it up, or we have received an TSO remove callback for the given instance handle (it will tick while blocking). If the timeout runs up before we get a remove, a TimeoutException will be thrown.

      • waitForTSORemovalTimeout

        public void waitForTSORemovalTimeout(int instanceHandle)
        This method is the inverse of waitForTSORemoval(int). Rather than waiting for the removal, and then failing the test if it does not occur, it waits for the timeout to occur, erroring if a TSO removal of the given instance occurs in that time.

      • waitForROInteraction

        public TestInteraction waitForROInteraction(int classHandle)
        This method will block until an RO interaction of the given class handle is received. If an appropriate interaction is not received in a timely fashion, a TimeoutException will be thrown. NOTE: interactions are stored up as they are received, so you may actually get an older interaction than you expect.

      • waitForROInteraction

        public TestInteraction waitForROInteraction(String className)
        This method is the same as waitForROInteraction(int), except that it will resolve the name of the class to a handle for you. If there is a problem doing this, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test.

      • waitForROInteractionTimeout

        public void waitForROInteractionTimeout(int classHandle)
        This method is the rough inverse of the waitForROInteraction(int) method. It will wait for the timeout period for an RO interaction of the given class handle to be received, however, it is expecting a timeout rather than to actually receive an interaction. If the wait times out as desired, the method will return happily. If however an interaction of the correct type is received, Assert.fail() will be used to kill the test.

      • waitForROInteractionTimeout
